newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic, MCI interconnect in 2 states.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic, MCI interconnect in 2 states.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said Thursday it had signed deals with MCI Communications Corp allowing MCI to interconnect to Bell Atlantic's local network and resell local phone services in two states.
In addtion, MCI will be allowed to purchase and combine "unbundled network elements" of Bell Atlantic's network to create new services of MCI's own choosing.
The company said the interconnection agreements cover New Jersey and Pennsylvania. They expand on interim interconnection pacts the two companies had signed previously.
Under the resale deals, MCI will resell Bell Atlantic local service under the MCI brand.

The "unbundled elements" in the deal include providing MCI access to Bell Atlantic databases and ordering systems, co-location of MCI network equipment at Bell Atlantic central offices and number portablility, among other features.

Federal regulatiors are requiring that Regional Bell companies such as Bell Atlantic negotiate these interconnection pacts with competitors before Bell Atlantic will be permitted to offer long distance services in its service region.
MCI will pay Bell Atlantic prices based on the actual cost of providing the services, Bell Atlantic said.
The rates are expected to be approved by the Pennsylvania Public Utilties Commission Thursday and by the New Jersey Board of Public Utitlies shortly, Bell Atlantic said.
MCI is in a pact to merge with British Telecommunications Plc and Bell Atlantic has agreed to merge with NYNEX Corp.
